input.quote: 3.19 Exclusivity Commitment of SFJ. During the applicable Exclusive Period, SFJ shall not, and shall cause its Affiliates not to, either by itself or through a Third Party, conduct human clinical trials of, or sell, offer for sale or have sold:
input.rationale: The only exclusivity/field-of-use covenant in the Agreement (Section 3.19, read with the "Exclusive Period", "Competing Product" and "Brilinta Competing Product" definitions) binds SFJ, the counterparty, not PB — it restricts SFJ from running trials of or selling ticagrelor-reversal and competing P2Y12 products, which operates in our favour. A search of the covenants (Sections 7.5–7.6), the definitions and Article 14 shows no provision preventing PB from developing, acquiring, manufacturing or commercialising any competing or alternative product, and no post-term restriction on our business. Section 7.5.5 requires SFJ consent for certain Licensing Transactions concerning the Product, but that is a financing/collateral protection over our own out-licensing of the funded Product rather than a non-compete or field-of-use restriction on the businesses we may operate or the products we may buy or build, so it is not treated under this rule. This meets the preferred position: no non-compete on the Customer.
